summaries.text: This file serves as the package initializer for the `app` module [[target/app/__init__.py]]. As an `__init__.py`, it marks the `app` directory as a Python package, making its submodules and components importable by the rest of the codebase [[target/app/__init__.py]].

This file serves as the package initializer for the `app/api` module, marking the directory as a Python package and making it importable as `app.api` [[target/app/api/__init__.py]]. It does not define any functions, classes, or top-level logic of its own; its role is purely structural, providing the namespace entry point through which the API layer's submodules and routers can be organized and accessed [[target/app/api/__init__.py]].

This file is empty — it serves solely as a Python package marker, making the `dependencies` directory importable as a package [[target/app/api/dependencies/__init__.py]]. It defines no functions, classes, or other symbols of its own [[target/app/api/dependencies/__init__.py]].

Verifies that the currently authenticated user has permission to modify a given article, raising an `HTTPException` with HTTP 403 Forbidden if the check fails [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]]. It resolves the target article via `get_article_by_slug_from_path` and the acting user via `get_current_user_authorizer`, both injected through FastAPI's `Depends` mechanism [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. The authorization decision is delegated to `check_user_can_modify_article`, and when that returns falsy the exception is raised with a detail message drawn from the `strings` module [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]].

Fetches an article by its URL path slug, delegating to `articles_repo.get_article_by_slug` with the slug and the optionally authenticated user [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]]. The slug is extracted from the request path and must be at least one character long [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]]. Authentication is optional, resolved via `get_current_user_authorizer(required=False)`, meaning the endpoint is accessible to anonymous users but will pass along the identity of an authenticated one [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. The repository is injected through `get_repository(ArticlesRepository)` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. If no matching article exists, the caught `EntityDoesNotExist` exception is re-raised as an HTTP 404 [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]].

Collects optional query-string filters (`tag`, `author`, `favorited`) and validated pagination parameters (`limit`, `offset`) from the request, enforcing a minimum of 1 for `limit` and 0 for `offset` via FastAPI's `Query` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]]. It packages all five values into an `ArticlesFilters` object and returns it [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]].

Delegates to the parent class's `__call__` implementation by awaiting `super().__call__(request)` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]]. If the parent raises a `StarletteHTTPException`, it is caught and re-raised as a `HTTPException` with the same status code but with the detail message replaced by `strings.AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]].

Extracts and validates the Bearer-style token from an incoming API key header by splitting the raw header value on a space and returning the token portion [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]]. It depends on `get_app_settings` to retrieve the configured JWT token prefix used for comparison [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]]. If the header value cannot be split into exactly two parts, it raises an `HTTPException` with HTTP 403 [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]]. If the prefix portion does not match `settings.jwt_token_prefix`, it raises a second `HTTPException` with HTTP 403 [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]]. On success, the bare token string (without the prefix) is returned [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]].

When an `Authorization` header is present, it delegates to `_get_authorization_header` to validate and extract the token, forwarding both the raw header value and the injected application settings [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_optional]]. When no header is supplied, it returns an empty string rather than raising an error, making the credential optional [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_optional]]. Application settings are provided via `get_app_settings` [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]], and the header is read without forcing an error on absence thanks to `RWAPIKeyHeader` configured with `auto_error=False` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_optional]].

Returns `_get_authorization_header` when `required` is `True`, or `_get_authorization_header_optional` when `required` is `False`, acting as a factory that selects the appropriate authorization header retriever based on whether the header is mandatory [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]].

Decodes the JWT `token` using the app's secret key to extract a username, raising an `HTTPException` with status 403 if the token payload is malformed [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]] [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]]. If the token is valid, it fetches and returns the corresponding `User` from the database via `users_repo` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. A second `HTTPException` with status 403 is raised if no user matching the extracted username exists in the repository [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]].

Resolves the current user from an optional Bearer token, returning `None` when no token is present rather than raising an error [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user_optional]]. It injects a `UsersRepository` via `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]], retrieves an authorization header through `_get_authorization_header_retriever` configured with `required=False` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]], and receives application settings via `get_app_settings` [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]]. When a token is present, it delegates to `_get_current_user` with the repository, token, and settings to perform the actual lookup and return a `User` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user_optional]].

Returns `_get_current_user` when `required` is `True` (the default), or `_get_current_user_optional` when `required` is `False`, allowing callers to select between mandatory and optional authentication [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. The returned `Callable` is intended for use as a FastAPI dependency that enforces or relaxes the authentication requirement depending on the route [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py]].

Resolves a `Comment` via [`get_comment_by_id_from_path`](target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path) and the currently authenticated `User` via [`get_current_user_authorizer`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer) as FastAPI dependencies [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. It calls `check_user_can_modify_comment` with those two values to determine whether the user has permission to modify the comment [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. If the check fails, it raises an `HTTPException` with a `403 Forbidden` status and a "user is not author" detail message [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]].

Fetches a single comment by its integer path parameter `comment_id` (minimum value 1), scoped to the article resolved from the URL slug [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]]. It resolves the parent article via `get_article_by_slug_from_path` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]] and optionally identifies the requesting user through `get_current_user_authorizer(required=False)`, meaning authentication is not mandatory [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. The `CommentsRepository` is injected via `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]], and the actual database lookup is delegated to `comments_repo.get_comment_by_id` with all three resolved values passed as arguments [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]]. If the comment does not exist, `EntityDoesNotExist` is caught and re-raised as an `HTTPException` with a 404 status code [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]].

Acquires a database connection from the pool using `pool.acquire()` and yields it to the caller as an async context manager, returning it to the pool automatically when the caller is done [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_connection_from_pool]]. The `pool` parameter is injected by FastAPI's dependency system via `_get_db_pool` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_db_pool]].

Retrieves the database connection pool attached to the application state [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_db_pool]] by reading `request.app.state.pool` and returning it directly to the caller [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_db_pool]].

A factory that accepts a `BaseRepository` subclass and returns a FastAPI-compatible dependency function [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. The inner function uses `Depends` to inject a database connection obtained from the connection pool, then instantiates the requested repository type with that connection [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. The returned callable closes over `repo_type` so each call produces a fresh repository instance bound to the resolved connection [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]].

Fetches a [`Profile`](target/app/api/dependencies/profiles.py) for the `username` extracted from the URL path (minimum length 1), passing the optionally authenticated `user` as the requesting context to `profiles_repo.get_profile_by_username` so that follow/unfollow state can be resolved [[target/app/api/dependencies/profiles.py::get_profile_by_username_from_path]]. The current user is resolved via [`get_current_user_authorizer`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer) with `required=False`, meaning the endpoint is accessible without authentication [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. The `profiles_repo` dependency is injected by [`get_repository`](target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository), which supplies a `ProfilesRepository` bound to the active database session [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. If the requested username does not exist, `EntityDoesNotExist` is caught and re-raised as an `HTTPException` with status 404 [[target/app/api/dependencies/profiles.py::get_profile_by_username_from_path]].

The file [`target/app/api/errors/__init__.py`](target/app/api/errors/__init__.py) is an empty package initialiser that marks the `errors` directory as a Python package [[target/app/api/errors/__init__.py]]. It contains no definitions of its own, serving purely as a namespace anchor so that sibling or child modules within the `errors` package can be imported using the `app.api.errors` path [[target/app/api/errors/__init__.py]].

Accepts a request (ignored) and an `HTTPException`, then wraps the exception's detail in an `{"errors": [...]}` list and returns a `JSONResponse` using the exception's status code [[target/app/api/errors/http_error.py::http_error_handler]].

Accepts a `Request` (ignored) and either a `RequestValidationError` or `ValidationError` exception, then calls `exc.errors()` to extract the validation error details and wraps them in a `{"errors": ...}` envelope returned as a `JSONResponse` with HTTP status 422 Unprocessable Entity [[target/app/api/errors/validation_error.py::http422_error_handler]].

This file serves as the package initializer for the `app.api.routes` module, marking the directory as a Python package [[target/app/api/routes/__init__.py]]. It does not define any functions, classes, or exports of its own, but its presence allows other parts of the application to import from the `routes` package [[target/app/api/routes/__init__.py]].

This module serves as the top-level API router that assembles all feature-specific sub-routers into a single `APIRouter` instance for the application [[target/app/api/routes/api.py]]. A root `router` object is created and then extended by mounting six sub-routers, each scoped to its own URL prefix and tag: authentication routes are mounted under `/users`, user routes under `/user`, profile routes under `/profiles`, article routes without an additional prefix, comment routes under `/articles/{slug}/comments`, and tag routes under `/tags` [[target/app/api/routes/api.py]]. By centralising all `include_router` calls here, this file acts as the single wiring point that connects every domain area of the API into one coherent router, which the application can register in one step [[target/app/api/routes/api.py]].

This file serves as the package initializer for the `articles` route module within the API [[target/app/api/routes/articles/__init__.py]]. As an `__init__.py`, its primary role is to mark the `articles` directory as a Python package, making its contents importable by the rest of the application [[target/app/api/routes/articles/__init__.py]].

This file serves as the top-level article routing aggregator for the API, combining two sub-routers into a single unified `APIRouter` instance [[target/app/api/routes/articles/api.py]]. It imports from both `articles_common` and `articles_resource` and mounts each under the `/articles` prefix, so all article-related endpoints are grouped together and exposed through one router [[target/app/api/routes/articles/api.py]]. The resulting `router` object is what gets registered elsewhere in the application to activate all article routes [[target/app/api/routes/articles/api.py]].

Handles `GET /api/articles/feed` by fetching the authenticated user's personalised article feed [[route:GET /api/articles/feed]] [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::get_articles_for_user_feed]]. It requires a valid authenticated user via [`get_current_user_authorizer()`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer) and an `ArticlesRepository` instance supplied by [`get_repository`](target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository). Pagination is controlled by `limit` (minimum 1, defaults to `DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT`) and `offset` (minimum 0, defaults to `DEFAULT_ARTICLES_OFFSET`) [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::get_articles_for_user_feed]]. It delegates the database query to `articles_repo.get_articles_for_user_feed`, passing the resolved `user`, `limit`, and `offset` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::get_articles_for_user_feed]]. Each returned article is converted to an `ArticleForResponse` via its `.dict()` representation, then the full list is wrapped in a [`ListOfArticlesInResponse`](target/app/models/schemas/articles.py::ListOfArticlesInResponse) that also carries the total count [[target/app/models/schemas/articles.py::ListOfArticlesInResponse]].

Handles `POST /api/articles/{slug}/favorite` to mark an article as a favourite for the authenticated user [[route:POST /api/articles/{slug}/favorite]] [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::mark_article_as_favorite]]. The article is resolved from the URL slug via `get_article_by_slug_from_path` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]], the acting user is supplied by `get_current_user_authorizer` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]], and the repository is injected through `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. When the article is not yet favourited, it calls `articles_repo.add_article_into_favorites` to persist the relationship and returns an `ArticleInResponse` whose embedded article reflects `favorited: True` and an incremented `favorites_count` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::mark_article_as_favorite]] [[target/app/models/schemas/articles.py::ArticleInResponse]]. If the article is already favourited, it raises `HTTPException` with HTTP 400 [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::mark_article_as_favorite]].

Handles `DELETE /api/articles/{slug}/favorite` to remove an article from the current user's favorites [[route:DELETE /api/articles/{slug}/favorite]] [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::remove_article_from_favorites]]. The article is resolved from the URL slug via `get_article_by_slug_from_path` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]], the authenticated user is injected by `get_current_user_authorizer` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]], and the repository is provided by `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. When `article.favorited` is `True`, it calls `articles_repo.remove_article_from_favorites` then builds and returns an `ArticleInResponse` whose embedded article has `favorited` patched to `False` and `favorites_count` decremented by one [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::remove_article_from_favorites]] [[target/app/models/schemas/articles.py::ArticleInResponse]]. If the article is not already favorited, it raises `HTTPException` with status `400 Bad Request` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::remove_article_from_favorites]].

Handles the `POST /api/articles` route to create a new article on behalf of an authenticated user [[route:POST /api/articles]] [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::create_new_article]]. It accepts the article payload as an embedded request body under the key `"article"`, typed as `ArticleInCreate` [[target/app/models/schemas/articles.py::ArticleInCreate]], and resolves the current user and the articles repository via FastAPI dependency injection [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. A URL-safe slug is derived from the incoming title, then the repository is queried to check whether an article with that slug already exists; if it does, an `HTTPException` with status `400` is raised [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::create_new_article]]. When the slug is free, the article is persisted via `articles_repo.create_article`, passing the slug, title, description, body, authenticated user as author, and tags [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::create_new_article]]. The persisted article is wrapped with `ArticleForResponse.from_orm` and returned inside an `ArticleInResponse` envelope [[target/app/models/schemas/articles.py::ArticleInResponse]].

Handles the `DELETE /api/articles/{slug}` route, responding with HTTP 204 No Content on success [[route:DELETE /api/articles/{slug}]] [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::delete_article_by_slug]]. The target article is resolved from the URL slug via `get_article_by_slug_from_path` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]], and `check_article_modification_permissions` is enforced as a route-level dependency before the handler body executes [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]]. An `ArticlesRepository` is injected through `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]], and the resolved article is permanently deleted by delegating to `articles_repo.delete_article` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::delete_article_by_slug]].

Handles `GET /api/articles` and returns a paginated, filtered list of articles wrapped in a `ListOfArticlesInResponse` envelope [[route:GET /api/articles]] [[target/app/models/schemas/articles.py::ListOfArticlesInResponse]]. It resolves filtering parameters (tag, author, favorited, limit, offset) via `get_articles_filters` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]], an optional authenticated user via `get_current_user_authorizer(required=False)` so unauthenticated callers are permitted [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]], and the article repository via `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. It calls `articles_repo.filter_articles` with all resolved filter values and the optional `requested_user`, then maps each result through `ArticleForResponse.from_orm` before constructing the final response with both the article list and its count [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::list_articles]].

Handles `GET /api/articles/{slug}` requests, resolving the target article via the `get_article_by_slug_from_path` dependency injected into the `article` parameter [[route:GET /api/articles/{slug}]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]]. It converts the resolved `Article` ORM object into a response-safe form using `ArticleForResponse.from_orm`, wraps it in an `ArticleInResponse`, and returns it [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::retrieve_article_by_slug]] [[target/app/models/schemas/articles.py::ArticleInResponse]].

Handles `PUT /api/articles/{slug}` to update an existing article [[route:PUT /api/articles/{slug}]] [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::update_article_by_slug]]. The update payload is accepted as an embedded body field aliased to `"article"` and typed as `ArticleInUpdate` [[target/app/models/schemas/articles.py::ArticleInUpdate]]. The article to be modified is resolved from the URL slug via `get_article_by_slug_from_path` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]], and write access is enforced before the handler runs via the `check_article_modification_permissions` dependency [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]]. A new slug is derived from the updated title when a title is provided, otherwise `None` is passed [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::update_article_by_slug]]. The resolved slug and the remaining update fields (spread from `article_update.dict()`) are forwarded to `articles_repo.update_article`, which is injected via `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. The updated article is then wrapped with `ArticleForResponse.from_orm` and returned inside an `ArticleInResponse` envelope [[target/app/models/schemas/articles.py::ArticleInResponse]].

Handles `POST /api/users/login` requests, accepting login credentials embedded in the request body under the `user` key [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::login]] [[target/app/models/schemas/users.py::UserInLogin]]. It fetches the matching account by email via `users_repo.get_user_by_email`; if no account exists, it raises an `HTTP 400` error [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::login]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. If the account is found but `user.check_password` returns false for the supplied password, the same `HTTP 400` error is raised [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::login]]. On success it mints a JWT via `jwt.create_access_token_for_user`, using the secret retrieved from `settings.secret_key.get_secret_value()` [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::login]] [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]]. It returns a `UserInResponse` wrapping a `UserWithToken` that carries the user's username, email, bio, image, and the newly created token [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::login]] [[target/app/models/schemas/users.py::UserInResponse]].

Handles `POST /api/users` and returns a newly created user with a JWT access token [[route:POST /api/users]] [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::register]]. Accepts the new user's details as a `UserInCreate` body (embedded under the `"user"` key) [[target/app/models/schemas/users.py::UserInCreate]]. Before creating the user, it checks whether the requested username is already taken and raises `HTTPException` with HTTP 400 if so [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::register]]; it then performs the same uniqueness check for the email address and raises a second `HTTPException` with HTTP 400 if that is taken [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::register]]. Once both checks pass it persists the new user via `users_repo.create_user`, which is injected through `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. It then mints a JWT by calling `jwt.create_access_token_for_user` with the created user and the application secret, which is retrieved from injected `AppSettings` via `settings.secret_key.get_secret_value()` [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]]. The response is a `UserInResponse` wrapping a `UserWithToken` that carries the username, email, bio, image, and the newly issued token [[target/app/models/schemas/users.py::UserInResponse]].

Handles `POST /api/articles/{slug}/comments`, creating a new comment and returning it wrapped in a `CommentInResponse` [[route:POST /api/articles/{slug}/comments]] [[target/app/api/routes/comments.py::create_comment_for_article]]. The comment body is read from the request as a `CommentInCreate` instance embedded under the key `"comment"` [[target/app/models/schemas/comments.py::CommentInCreate]]. The target article is resolved from the URL slug via `get_article_by_slug_from_path` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]], and the authenticated user is injected by `get_current_user_authorizer` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. A `CommentsRepository` instance is provided through `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. It delegates persistence to `comments_repo.create_comment_for_article`, passing the comment body, article, and user, then wraps the result in a `CommentInResponse` and returns it with HTTP 201 [[target/app/api/routes/comments.py::create_comment_for_article]] [[target/app/models/schemas/comments.py::CommentInResponse]].

Handles `DELETE /api/articles/{slug}/comments/{comment_id}` and returns HTTP 204 No Content on success [[route:DELETE /api/articles/{slug}/comments/{comment_id}]] [[target/app/api/routes/comments.py::delete_comment_from_article]]. The target comment is resolved from the path via `get_comment_by_id_from_path`, and a `CommentsRepository` instance is injected via `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. Before the handler body runs, `check_comment_modification_permissions` is enforced as a FastAPI dependency, guarding the route against unauthorised callers [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. The sole side effect is an awaited call to `comments_repo.delete_comment`, passing the resolved comment, which performs the actual deletion [[target/app/api/routes/comments.py::delete_comment_from_article]].

Handles `GET /api/articles/{slug}/comments`, returning all comments for a given article wrapped in a [`ListOfCommentsInResponse`](target/app/models/schemas/comments.py::ListOfCommentsInResponse) [[route:GET /api/articles/{slug}/comments]] [[target/app/models/schemas/comments.py::ListOfCommentsInResponse]]. The article is resolved from the URL slug via `get_article_by_slug_from_path` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]], and an optional authenticated user is resolved via `get_current_user_authorizer(required=False)`, meaning authentication is accepted but not enforced [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. A `CommentsRepository` is injected through `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. It awaits `comments_repo.get_comments_for_article` with the resolved article and optional user, then constructs and returns a [`ListOfCommentsInResponse`](target/app/models/schemas/comments.py::ListOfCommentsInResponse) from the result [[target/app/api/routes/comments.py::list_comments_for_article]] [[target/app/models/schemas/comments.py::ListOfCommentsInResponse]].

Handles `POST /api/profiles/{username}/follow` to let an authenticated user follow another profile [[route:POST /api/profiles/{username}/follow]] [[target/app/api/routes/profiles.py::follow_for_user]]. This module is a central registry of human-readable API error and status message strings used throughout the application [[target/app/resources/strings.py]]. It defines a flat collection of module-level string constants, each corresponding to a specific error or boundary condition that the API may need to communicate to a client [[target/app/resources/strings.py]].

The constants cover several distinct concern areas. User-related errors include messages for a missing user, duplicate username or email at registration, and incorrect login credentials [[target/app/resources/strings.py]]. Article-related errors cover cases where an article does not exist, already exists, has already been favorited, is not currently favorited, or where the requesting user is not its author [[target/app/resources/strings.py]]. Follow/subscription errors describe attempts to follow or unfollow oneself, following a user that is already followed, and unfollowing a user that is not currently followed [[target/app/resources/strings.py]]. Authentication errors handle an unsupported authorization prefix, a payload that cannot be validated, and a general authentication-required condition [[target/app/resources/strings.py]]. Finally, a comment error constant covers the case where a requested comment does not exist [[target/app/resources/strings.py]].

By centralising all these literals in one place, the module ensures that any code path raising or returning one of these messages can import it by name rather than repeating the raw string, keeping error text consistent and easy to update in a single location [[target/app/resources/strings.py]].

Accepts an `ArticlesRepository` and a slug string, then attempts to fetch the matching article by calling `articles_repo.get_article_by_slug` [[target/app/services/articles.py::check_article_exists]]. Accepts a `User` object and a `secret_key` string, then constructs a JWT payload by extracting the username into a `JWTUser` struct and serialising it to a dictionary [[target/app/services/jwt.py::create_access_token_for_user]]. Delegates token generation to `create_jwt_token`, passing the serialised payload, the secret key, and an expiry window derived from `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES` via `timedelta` [[target/app/services/jwt.py::create_access_token_for_user]]. Returns the resulting signed JWT string [[target/app/services/jwt.py::create_access_token_for_user]].

The augmented payload is signed and encoded into a JWT string using `secret_key` and the module-level `ALGORITHM` constant, and that string is returned [[target/app/services/jwt.py::create_jwt_token]].

This module provides FastAPI dependency functions used to resolve article-related concerns — lookup, filtering, and permission enforcement — for the articles API layer [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py]].

If no article matches the slug, the internal `EntityDoesNotExist` exception is translated into an HTTP 404 response [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]].

The `check_article_modification_permissions` dependency builds on `get_article_by_slug_from_path` by also requiring a fully authenticated user, then delegating the authorization decision to `check_user_can_modify_article` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]]. If that check fails, an HTTP 403 Forbidden exception is raised using a message from the `strings` resource module, ensuring that only permitted users can mutate an article [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]].

The `get_articles_filters` dependency operates independently of the other two, collecting up to five optional query-string parameters — a tag, an author name, a favorited-by username, and pagination `limit` and `offset` values — and packing them into a single `ArticlesFilters` object that callers can consume [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]]. Minimum bounds are enforced by FastAPI's `Query` validator before the object is constructed [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]].

`RWAPIKeyHeader` is a subclass of FastAPI's external `APIKeyHeader` security class [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader]]. It is not a Pydantic model and declares no additional fields of its own [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader]]. Its sole behavioural addition is an overridden `__call__` method that delegates to the parent's `__call__` implementation by awaiting `super().__call__(request)` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]]. When the parent raises a `StarletteHTTPException`, the override catches it and re-raises it as an `HTTPException` carrying the same status code but with the detail message replaced by `strings.AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`, giving the application a consistent, application-level error response for missing or invalid API keys [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]].

This module provides FastAPI dependency functions for resolving and authorizing comment resources in the API layer [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py]].

The first dependency, [`get_comment_by_id_from_path`](target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path), fetches a single comment by its integer path parameter `comment_id`, scoped to the article identified by the URL slug [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]]. It resolves the parent article and optionally identifies the requesting user (authentication is not required), then delegates the actual database lookup to `CommentsRepository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]]. If no matching comment exists, it catches `EntityDoesNotExist` and re-raises it as an `HTTPException` with a 404 status code [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]].

The second dependency, [`check_comment_modification_permissions`](target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions), builds directly on [`get_comment_by_id_from_path`](target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path) by declaring it as a FastAPI dependency alongside the currently authenticated user [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. It passes both the resolved comment and the authenticated user to `check_user_can_modify_comment` to determine whether the operation is permitted [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. If that check fails, it raises an `HTTPException` with a 403 Forbidden status and a "user is not author" detail message, preventing unauthorized modifications [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]].

Together, the two functions form a layered authorization chain: the first handles resource resolution and existence checks, while the second enforces ownership rules on top of the resolved resource [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py]].

This module provides FastAPI dependency functions that wire database connectivity into route handlers [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py]]. It imports FastAPI's `Depends`, asyncpg's `Connection` and `Pool` types, and the project's `BaseRepository` to build a layered dependency chain [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py]].

The chain starts with `_get_db_pool`, which retrieves the application-level connection pool by reading `request.app.state.pool` and returning it directly to its caller [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_db_pool]]. One level up, `_get_connection_from_pool` takes that pool — injected automatically by FastAPI via `_get_db_pool` — and acquires a single connection from it using `pool.acquire()`, yielding the connection as an async context manager so it is returned to the pool as soon as the request finishes [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_connection_from_pool]].

At the top of the chain sits `get_repository`, a factory function that accepts any `BaseRepository` subclass and produces a FastAPI-compatible dependency function ready to be used with `Depends` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. The inner function it returns injects a live database connection through the pool chain and instantiates the requested repository type with that connection, so each request receives a fresh repository instance bound to its own connection [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]]. Because the inner function closes over the `repo_type` argument, a single call to `get_repository` can be reused across many routes while always producing the correct repository type [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]].

This module serves as a FastAPI dependency provider for profile-related operations, exposing a single injectable function that resolves a user profile from the current request context [[target/app/api/dependencies/profiles.py]].

The function [`get_profile_by_username_from_path`](target/app/api/dependencies/profiles.py::get_profile_by_username_from_path) reads the `username` segment directly from the URL path (enforcing a minimum length of 1) and delegates to `profiles_repo.get_profile_by_username` to retrieve the corresponding [`Profile`](target/app/api/dependencies/profiles.py), passing along the optionally authenticated caller so that follow/unfollow state can be resolved [[target/app/api/dependencies/profiles.py::get_profile_by_username_from_path]]. Authentication is intentionally optional: the current user is obtained via `get_current_user_authorizer(required=False)`, which means the endpoint remains accessible to unauthenticated callers while still enriching the response with relationship state when a valid user is present [[target/app/api/dependencies/profiles.py::get_profile_by_username_from_path]]. The `ProfilesRepository` itself is injected by `get_repository`, which binds the repository to the active database session for the duration of the request [[target/app/api/dependencies/profiles.py::get_profile_by_username_from_path]]. When the requested username cannot be found, the function catches `EntityDoesNotExist` and converts it into an `HTTPException` carrying HTTP 404, keeping the API error contract clean and consistent [[target/app/api/dependencies/profiles.py::get_profile_by_username_from_path]].

This module provides a custom HTTP error handler for a FastAPI application [[target/app/api/errors/http_error.py]]. It defines a single function, `http_error_handler`, which accepts an incoming request and an `HTTPException`, then formats the exception's detail into a structured `{"errors": [...]}` list and returns a `JSONResponse` carrying the exception's original status code [[target/app/api/errors/http_error.py::http_error_handler]]. The module imports `HTTPException` from FastAPI along with Starlette's `Request` and `JSONResponse` types, which are the building blocks that `http_error_handler` relies on to receive the error and produce a consistently shaped response [[target/app/api/errors/http_error.py]].

This module configures FastAPI's validation error handling by customising the OpenAPI response schema and providing a dedicated error handler [[target/app/api/errors/validation_error.py]]. At module level, it patches `validation_error_response_definition["properties"]` to replace the default schema with a single `"errors"` array whose items reference the standard `ValidationError` OpenAPI component, ensuring the generated API documentation accurately reflects the error envelope shape [[target/app/api/errors/validation_error.py]]. The central function, `http422_error_handler`, accepts a `Request` (which it ignores) alongside either a `RequestValidationError` or a `ValidationError`, calls `exc.errors()` to extract the structured validation details, and returns them wrapped in a `{"errors": ...}` envelope as a `JSONResponse` with HTTP status 422 Unprocessable Entity [[target/app/api/errors/validation_error.py::http422_error_handler]]. Together, the module-level schema patch and the handler function ensure that both the runtime error response and the static OpenAPI documentation agree on the same `{"errors": [...]}` structure [[target/app/api/errors/validation_error.py]] [[target/app/api/errors/validation_error.py::http422_error_handler]].

This module defines a shared FastAPI `router` and three route handler functions that together cover the article feed and favouriting features of the API [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py]].

The first handler, `get_articles_for_user_feed`, serves `GET /api/articles/feed` and returns a paginated, personalised feed for the currently authenticated user [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::get_articles_for_user_feed]]. It accepts `limit` and `offset` query parameters (with sensible defaults drawn from `DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT` and `DEFAULT_ARTICLES_OFFSET`) and delegates the actual database retrieval to `ArticlesRepository`, wrapping the results in a `ListOfArticlesInResponse` that carries the total article count [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::get_articles_for_user_feed]].

The second handler, `mark_article_as_favorite`, serves `POST /api/articles/{slug}/favorite` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::mark_article_as_favorite]]. It resolves the target article from the URL slug, verifies the user is authenticated, and — provided the article is not already favourited — persists the relationship via the repository and returns an `ArticleInResponse` reflecting `favorited: True` and an incremented `favorites_count` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::mark_article_as_favorite]]. Attempting to favourite an already-favourited article results in an `HTTP 400` error [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::mark_article_as_favorite]].

The third handler, `remove_article_from_favorites`, mirrors that logic in reverse, serving `DELETE /api/articles/{slug}/favorite` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::remove_article_from_favorites]]. When the article is currently favourited it removes the relationship and returns an `ArticleInResponse` with `favorited` patched to `False` and `favorites_count` decremented by one; if the article was not favourited to begin with, it raises `HTTP 400` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::remove_article_from_favorites]].

All three handlers share the same dependency wiring pattern: the article (where applicable) is resolved from the path slug, the acting user is supplied by `get_current_user_authorizer`, and the `ArticlesRepository` is injected via `get_repository` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::get_articles_for_user_feed]] [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::mark_article_as_favorite]] [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_common.py::remove_article_from_favorites]].

This module defines the FastAPI `router` and the five route-handler functions that together implement the core articles REST API [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py]].

`list_articles` handles `GET /api/articles` and returns a paginated, filtered collection of articles wrapped in a `ListOfArticlesInResponse` envelope [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::list_articles]]. It accepts an optional authenticated caller so that unauthenticated requests are also permitted, resolves filter parameters (tag, author, favorited, limit, offset), and maps each result through `ArticleForResponse.from_orm` before building the final response [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::list_articles]].

`create_new_article` handles `POST /api/articles` and requires an authenticated user [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::create_new_article]]. It derives a URL-safe slug from the incoming title and raises an `HTTPException` with status `400` if an article with that slug already exists; otherwise it persists the article and returns it inside an `ArticleInResponse` envelope [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::create_new_article]].

`retrieve_article_by_slug` handles `GET /api/articles/{slug}`, resolving the target article from the URL path, converting it with `ArticleForResponse.from_orm`, and returning it wrapped in an `ArticleInResponse` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::retrieve_article_by_slug]].

`update_article_by_slug` handles `PUT /api/articles/{slug}` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::update_article_by_slug]]. Before the handler body executes, write-access is enforced by `check_article_modification_permissions`; a new slug is derived from the updated title when one is provided, and the remaining update fields are forwarded to the repository before the result is returned in an `ArticleInResponse` [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::update_article_by_slug]].

`delete_article_by_slug` handles `DELETE /api/articles/{slug}` and responds with HTTP 204 No Content [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::delete_article_by_slug]]. Like the update handler, it enforces `check_article_modification_permissions` as a route-level dependency before delegating the permanent removal to the articles repository [[target/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py::delete_article_by_slug]].

This module is the authentication route handler for the API, defining the `APIRouter` instance and the two endpoints responsible for user registration and login [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py]].

The `register` function handles `POST /api/users` requests, accepting new user details as a `UserInCreate` payload embedded under the `"user"` key [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::register]]. Before persisting anything, it validates uniqueness by checking whether the requested username is already taken and raising an `HTTP 400` error if so, then repeating the same check for the email address [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::register]]. Once both checks pass, it creates the user record via the injected `UsersRepository`, mints a JWT using `jwt.create_access_token_for_user` with the application secret retrieved from the injected `AppSettings`, and returns a `UserInResponse` wrapping a `UserWithToken` containing the user's username, email, bio, image, and the new token [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::register]].

The `login` function handles `POST /api/users/login`, accepting credentials embedded under the `"user"` key [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::login]]. It looks up the account by email through the injected `UsersRepository`; if no matching account exists, it raises an `HTTP 400` error, and raises the same error if the supplied password fails the `check_password` verification [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::login]]. On success it mints a JWT via `jwt.create_access_token_for_user` using the secret from `settings.secret_key.get_secret_value()`, and returns a `UserInResponse` wrapping a `UserWithToken` with the user's credentials and the freshly issued token [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::login]].

The two endpoints share the same structural pattern: both depend on a `UsersRepository` injected via `get_repository`, both retrieve application configuration through `get_app_settings`, and both produce a `UserInResponse` as their successful response [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::register]] [[target/app/api/routes/authentication.py::login]].

[`target/app/api/routes/comments.py`](target/app/api/routes/comments.py) defines the FastAPI router responsible for all comment-related HTTP endpoints, mounting three route handlers that together cover the full create/read/delete lifecycle for article comments [[target/app/api/routes/comments.py]].

The first handler, [`create_comment_for_article`](target/app/api/routes/comments.py::create_comment_for_article), serves `POST /api/articles/{slug}/comments` and is the only route that requires an authenticated user; it reads the comment body from the request as a `CommentInCreate` payload, resolves the target article from the URL slug, persists the new comment via `CommentsRepository`, and returns the result wrapped in a `CommentInResponse` with HTTP 201 [[target/app/api/routes/comments.py::create_comment_for_article]].

The second handler, [`list_comments_for_article`](target/app/api/routes/comments.py::list_comments_for_article), serves `GET /api/articles/{slug}/comments` and relaxes the authentication requirement — a caller may be authenticated or anonymous — resolving the article from the slug and delegating retrieval to `CommentsRepository`, then returning all comments wrapped in a `ListOfCommentsInResponse` [[target/app/api/routes/comments.py::list_comments_for_article]].

The third handler, [`delete_comment_from_article`](target/app/api/routes/comments.py::delete_comment_from_article), serves `DELETE /api/articles/{slug}/comments/{comment_id}` and enforces `check_comment_modification_permissions` as a dependency before the handler body runs, ensuring only authorised callers can proceed; it resolves the target comment from the path, delegates deletion to `CommentsRepository`, and responds with HTTP 204 No Content [[target/app/api/routes/comments.py::delete_comment_from_article]].

All three handlers share a common pattern: the article or comment is resolved from path parameters by dedicated dependency functions, a `CommentsRepository` instance is injected via `get_repository`, and the actual database work is fully delegated to that repository, keeping the route handlers thin [[target/app/api/routes/comments.py]].

This module defines the FastAPI router for user profile operations, registering three route handlers under the profiles API [[target/app/api/routes/profiles.py]].

The `retrieve_profile_by_username` function handles `GET /api/profiles/{username}` requests, resolving the target profile via the `get_profile_by_username_from_path` dependency and wrapping the result in a `ProfileInResponse` envelope before returning it [[target/app/api/routes/profiles.py::retrieve_profile_by_username]].

The `follow_for_user` function handles `POST /api/profiles/{username}/follow`, allowing an authenticated user to follow another profile [[target/app/api/routes/profiles.py::follow_for_user]]. It shares the same three dependencies as the other write operations — the path-resolved profile via `get_profile_by_username_from_path`, the acting user via `get_current_user_authorizer`, and a `ProfilesRepository` via `get_repository` — a pattern repeated across both mutation handlers [[target/app/api/routes/profiles.py::follow_for_user]]. Before recording the follow, it guards against two invalid states: the authenticated user attempting to follow themselves, and the profile already being followed, raising `HTTPException` with `HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST` in either case [[target/app/api/routes/profiles.py::follow_for_user]]. On success it calls `profiles_repo.add_user_into_followers` and returns a `ProfileInResponse` with `following` set to `True` [[target/app/api/routes/profiles.py::follow_for_user]].

The `unsubscribe_from_user` function mirrors this structure for `DELETE /api/profiles/{username}/follow`, applying the same self-action and precondition guards — raising `HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST` when the user tries to unfollow themselves or is not currently following the target [[target/app/api/routes/profiles.py::unsubscribe_from_user]]. On success it calls `profiles_repo.remove_user_from_followers` and returns a `ProfileInResponse` with `following` set to `False` [[target/app/api/routes/profiles.py::unsubscribe_from_user]].

This module defines the tags route for the API, creating a FastAPI `APIRouter` and registering a single endpoint on it [[target/app/api/routes/tags.py]]. It exposes a `get_all_tags` handler that responds to `GET /api/tags` requests, using FastAPI's dependency injection to receive a `TagsRepository` [[target/app/api/routes/tags.py::get_all_tags]]. The handler retrieves every tag from the database and returns the results wrapped in a `TagsInList` response object [[target/app/api/routes/tags.py::get_all_tags]].

This module is the API route handler for user-account operations, defining the FastAPI `router` and the two endpoint functions that serve the authenticated user resource [[target/app/api/routes/users.py]].

`retrieve_current_user` handles the `GET /api/user` endpoint and returns the currently authenticated user's profile [[target/app/api/routes/users.py::retrieve_current_user]]. The authenticated `User` object is resolved through FastAPI dependency injection via `get_current_user_authorizer`, and application settings are resolved via `get_app_settings` [[target/app/api/routes/users.py::retrieve_current_user]]. Using those inputs, the function mints a fresh JWT access token by calling `jwt.create_access_token_for_user` with the user and the secret key extracted from settings, then assembles the user's `username`, `email`, `bio`, and `image` together with the new token into a `UserWithToken`, which is returned wrapped in a `UserInResponse` [[target/app/api/routes/users.py::retrieve_current_user]].

`update_current_user` handles the `PUT /api/user` endpoint and applies profile changes to the same authenticated user [[target/app/api/routes/users.py::update_current_user]]. It accepts a `UserInUpdate` payload embedded under the `"user"` key in the request body, resolves the current user, a `UsersRepository` instance, and application settings through dependency injection [[target/app/api/routes/users.py::update_current_user]]. Before persisting anything, it enforces uniqueness constraints: if the incoming update contains a new username that differs from the existing one, it checks availability and raises an `HTTPException` with HTTP 400 if the username is already taken; it performs the same check for a changed email address [[target/app/api/routes/users.py::update_current_user]]. Once both checks pass, it writes the changes by calling `users_repo.update_user` with the current user and the flattened update fields [[target/app/api/routes/users.py::update_current_user]]. A fresh JWT is then minted for the updated user using the application's secret key, and the function returns a `UserInResponse` wrapping a `UserWithToken` that bundles the updated profile with the new token [[target/app/api/routes/users.py::update_current_user]].

The two functions share the same response shape — a `UserInResponse` containing a `UserWithToken` — and the same pattern of re-issuing a JWT on every successful request, ensuring the caller always receives a current token whether they are reading or updating their profile [[target/app/api/routes/users.py::retrieve_current_user]] [[target/app/api/routes/users.py::update_current_user]].

This module serves as the central configuration entry point for the application, mapping each supported environment type to its corresponding settings class and exposing a cached factory function for retrieving the active settings [[target/app/core/config.py]]. The `environments` dictionary ties the `AppEnvTypes` enum values — `dev`, `prod`, and `test` — to `DevAppSettings`, `ProdAppSettings`, and `TestAppSettings` respectively, so the correct settings class can be looked up by environment name [[target/app/core/config.py]].

The `get_app_settings` function acts as the single access point for application configuration: it reads the `app_env` field from a `BaseAppSettings` instance to identify the current environment, uses that value as a key into the `environments` mapping, and instantiates the matching settings class [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]]. Because it is decorated with `@lru_cache`, the instantiation happens only once and every subsequent call receives the same cached `AppSettings` object [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]]. This design means the rest of the application can call `get_app_settings` freely without repeatedly constructing settings objects or re-reading environment variables [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]].

This module serves as the FastAPI application lifecycle coordinator, providing factory functions that produce the startup and shutdown event handlers responsible for managing the database connection [[target/app/core/events.py]].

`create_start_app_handler` accepts a `FastAPI` application instance and an `AppSettings` configuration object, constructing and returning an inner async callable named `start_app` [[target/app/core/events.py::create_start_app_handler]]. When that callable is invoked during application startup, it establishes the database connection by delegating to `connect_to_db` with the same `app` and `settings` references [[target/app/core/events.py::create_start_app_handler]]. The returned `Callable` is designed to be registered directly as a startup event handler on the FastAPI application [[target/app/core/events.py]].

`create_stop_app_handler` mirrors this pattern for teardown: it accepts a `FastAPI` instance and returns a `Callable` that, when invoked, closes the application's database connection by delegating to `close_db_connection` [[target/app/core/events.py::create_stop_app_handler]]. The inner `stop_app` coroutine is decorated with `@logger.catch`, ensuring that any exception raised during shutdown is captured and logged rather than allowed to propagate [[target/app/core/events.py::create_stop_app_handler]].

Together, the two factory functions form a symmetric pair — one for opening and one for closing the database connection — giving the application a clean, handler-based contract for its full lifecycle [[target/app/core/events.py]].

`InterceptHandler` is a custom logging handler that extends the standard `logging.Handler` base class [[target/app/core/logging.py::InterceptHandler]]. It is not a Pydantic model and declares no fields of its own [[target/app/core/logging.py::InterceptHandler]]. Its sole responsibility is to act as a bridge between Python's built-in `logging` infrastructure and the Loguru logging library, routing any record emitted through the standard `logging` system into Loguru [[target/app/core/logging.py::InterceptHandler::emit]].

This bridging is performed entirely by its `emit` method, which accepts a standard `logging.LogRecord` and first resolves the corresponding Loguru level name from `record.levelname`, falling back to the numeric level string when no named Loguru level matches [[target/app/core/logging.py::InterceptHandler::emit]]. To ensure that Loguru reports the correct call site rather than an internal frame inside the `logging` module, `emit` walks the call stack upward from `logging.currentframe()`, incrementing a `depth` counter for every frame that still belongs to the standard `logging` machinery [[target/app/core/logging.py::InterceptHandler::emit]]. Finally, it invokes `logger.opt` with the computed `depth` and `record.exc_info` so that exception context is preserved, and forwards the resolved level together with the record's formatted message string through `logger.opt(depth=depth, exception=record.exc_info).log` [[target/app/core/logging.py::InterceptHandler::emit]].

`AppSettings` is a Pydantic model that holds the full runtime configuration for the application, inheriting from `BaseAppSettings` [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings]] [[target/app/core/settings/base.py::BaseAppSettings]]. It enables `validate_assignment`, meaning Pydantic re-validates field values whenever they are reassigned after construction [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings]].

The class carries fields covering four broad concerns [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings]]. For FastAPI application metadata it defines `debug` (default `False`), `docs_url` (default `"/docs"`), `openapi_prefix` (default `""`), `openapi_url` (default `"/openapi.json"`), `redoc_url` (default `"/redoc"`), `title` (default `"FastAPI example application"`), and `version` (default `"0.0.0"`) [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings]]. For the database it defines `database_url` as a `PostgresDsn` (required, no default), `max_connection_count` (default `10`), and `min_connection_count` (default `10`) [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings]]. For security it holds `secret_key` as a `SecretStr` (required, no default), `api_prefix` (default `"/api"`), `jwt_token_prefix` (default `"Token"`), and `allowed_hosts` as a `List[str]` (default `["*"]`) [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings]]. For logging it stores `logging_level` (default `logging.INFO`) and `loggers` as a `Tuple[str, str]` naming the two Uvicorn loggers (default `("uvicorn.asgi", "uvicorn.access")`) [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings]]. Additionally, `app_env` typed as `AppEnvTypes` with a default of `AppEnvTypes.prod` is inherited from `BaseAppSettings` [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings]] [[target/app/core/settings/base.py::BaseAppSettings]].

The `configure_logging` method replaces the root logger's handlers with a single `InterceptHandler` instance, attaches per-name `InterceptHandler` instances at `self.logging_level` to each logger named in `self.loggers`, and finally calls `logger.configure` to register a single sink pointing to `sys.stderr` at `self.logging_level` [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings::configure_logging]]. The `fastapi_kwargs` method assembles and returns a dictionary mapping `debug`, `docs_url`, `openapi_prefix`, `openapi_url`, `redoc_url`, `title`, and `version` to their current field values, intended to be unpacked directly as keyword arguments when the FastAPI application is constructed [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings::fastapi_kwargs]] [[target/app/core/settings/app.py::AppSettings]].

This module defines the foundational settings infrastructure for the application, combining an environment enumeration with a base Pydantic configuration class [[target/app/core/settings/base.py]].

`AppEnvTypes` is a plain Python `Enum` subclass that enumerates the three deployment environments the application recognises: `prod`, `dev`, and `test`, each holding a matching string value [[target/app/core/settings/base.py::AppEnvTypes]]. It carries no additional fields or methods beyond these three constants [[target/app/core/settings/base.py::AppEnvTypes]].

`BaseAppSettings` inherits from Pydantic's `BaseSettings` and acts as the root configuration class that environment-specific settings classes are expected to build upon [[target/app/core/settings/base.py::BaseAppSettings]]. It declares a single field, `app_env`, typed as `AppEnvTypes` with a default of `AppEnvTypes.prod`, directly tying the two definitions in this module together [[target/app/core/settings/base.py::BaseAppSettings]]. An inner `Config` class instructs Pydantic to populate field values from a `.env` file, allowing deployment environment to be controlled without changing source code [[target/app/core/settings/base.py]].

This module defines the development environment configuration for the FastAPI application [[target/app/core/settings/development.py]]. It imports Python's `logging` module and `AppSettings` from the application's core settings, then provides a single class that tailors those base settings for local development use [[target/app/core/settings/development.py]].

The sole component defined here is `DevAppSettings`, a Pydantic model that extends `AppSettings` and supplies development-specific defaults [[target/app/core/settings/development.py::DevAppSettings]]. It overrides three fields from the base class: `debug` is set to `True`, `title` is set to `"Dev FastAPI example application"`, and `logging_level` is set to `logging.DEBUG` so that verbose output is produced during development [[target/app/core/settings/development.py::DevAppSettings]]. An inner `Config` class inherits from `AppSettings.Config` and points to a `.env` file, allowing environment variables to be loaded from disk when running in development mode [[target/app/core/settings/development.py]].

All remaining configuration fields — including database connection parameters, API routing prefixes, JWT settings, allowed hosts, and logger names — are inherited unchanged from `AppSettings` and remain fully available on `DevAppSettings` [[target/app/core/settings/development.py::DevAppSettings]].

This module defines the production-specific settings class for the application [[target/app/core/settings/production.py]]. It imports `AppSettings` from the core settings package and exposes a single class, `ProdAppSettings`, which specialises that base class for the production environment [[target/app/core/settings/production.py::ProdAppSettings]].

`ProdAppSettings` is a Pydantic model that extends `AppSettings` and overrides the inner `Config` class to load environment variables from a `prod.env` file, making it the authoritative source of configuration when the application runs in production [[target/app/core/settings/production.py::ProdAppSettings]]. All of its fields are inherited directly from `AppSettings` rather than redefined here [[target/app/core/settings/production.py::ProdAppSettings]]. General application metadata is covered by `title`, `version`, `debug`, `docs_url`, `openapi_url`, `redoc_url`, and `openapi_prefix` [[target/app/core/settings/production.py::ProdAppSettings]]. Database connectivity is configured through `database_url` (a `PostgresDsn` with no default, meaning it must be supplied by the environment), together with `max_connection_count` and `min_connection_count` [[target/app/core/settings/production.py::ProdAppSettings]]. Security is handled by `secret_key` (a `SecretStr` that likewise carries no default) and `jwt_token_prefix` [[target/app/core/settings/production.py::ProdAppSettings]]. Routing and host allowances are controlled by `api_prefix` and `allowed_hosts` [[target/app/core/settings/production.py::ProdAppSettings]]. Logging behaviour is governed by `logging_level` and the `loggers` tuple [[target/app/core/settings/production.py::ProdAppSettings]]. Finally, `app_env` is set to `AppEnvTypes.prod`, explicitly marking this class as targeting the production environment and distinguishing it from any development or test counterparts [[target/app/core/settings/production.py::ProdAppSettings]].

This module defines the test-environment configuration for the application, importing the necessary types and the base settings class to support a single override model [[target/app/core/settings/test.py]].

`TestAppSettings` is a Pydantic model that extends `AppSettings` and provides a fixed, test-oriented configuration for the application [[target/app/core/settings/test.py::TestAppSettings]]. It overrides several fields with safe, predictable defaults suitable for a test environment, ensuring that tests run against a known, controlled baseline rather than production values [[target/app/core/settings/test.py::TestAppSettings]]. Specifically, `debug` defaults to `True` and `title` is set to `"Test FastAPI example application"`, while `secret_key` is hardcoded as a `SecretStr` holding `"test_secret"` [[target/app/core/settings/test.py::TestAppSettings]]. The `database_url` field is typed as `PostgresDsn` but carries no default, meaning it must be supplied by the test environment at runtime [[target/app/core/settings/test.py::TestAppSettings]]. Both `max_connection_count` and `min_connection_count` are fixed at `5`, and `logging_level` defaults to `logging.DEBUG` so that all log output is visible during test runs [[target/app/core/settings/test.py::TestAppSettings]]. All remaining fields — including `docs_url`, `openapi_prefix`, `openapi_url`, `redoc_url`, `version`, `api_prefix`, `jwt_token_prefix`, `allowed_hosts`, `loggers`, and `app_env` — are inherited directly from `AppSettings` and retain their own defaults [[target/app/core/settings/test.py::TestAppSettings]].

The [`errors.py`](target/app/db/errors.py) module serves as the home for database-layer exception types used across the application [[target/app/db/errors.py]]. It defines a single custom exception, `EntityDoesNotExist`, which extends Python's built-in `Exception` and carries no additional fields or methods beyond what it inherits [[target/app/db/errors.py::EntityDoesNotExist]]. Its sole responsibility is to signal that a requested entity could not be found in the database, making it a lightweight sentinel rather than a data-carrying object [[target/app/db/errors.py::EntityDoesNotExist]].

This module manages the lifecycle of the asyncpg database connection pool for the FastAPI application [[target/app/db/events.py]]. It defines two functions that are intended to be called at application startup and shutdown respectively [[target/app/db/events.py::connect_to_db]] [[target/app/db/events.py::close_db_connection]].

The `connect_to_db` function establishes an asyncpg connection pool and attaches it to `app.state.pool` so the rest of the application can access it [[target/app/db/events.py::connect_to_db]]. It derives the pool configuration from an `AppSettings` instance, converting `settings.database_url` to a string and passing `settings.min_connection_count` and `settings.max_connection_count` as the lower and upper bounds for the pool size [[target/app/db/events.py::connect_to_db]]. Progress is recorded via `logger.info` both before and after the pool is created [[target/app/db/events.py::connect_to_db]].

The `close_db_connection` function handles the complementary teardown: it logs a message, closes the pool stored on the application state, and logs a confirmation once the shutdown is complete [[target/app/db/events.py::close_db_connection]]. Together the two functions ensure the connection pool is cleanly opened and closed around the application's lifespan [[target/app/db/events.py::connect_to_db]] [[target/app/db/events.py::close_db_connection]].

`Parameter` is a subclass of `CommonParameter` defined in the query-building module [[target/app/db/queries/tables.py]]. It is not a Pydantic model [[target/app/db/queries/tables.py::Parameter]]. Its sole responsibility is to produce asyncpg-style numbered placeholders (such as `$1` or `$2`) for use in dynamically constructed SQL queries [[target/app/db/queries/tables.py::Parameter]].

Construction is handled entirely by [`__init__`](target/app/db/queries/tables.py::Parameter::__init__), which accepts a single integer argument `count` and immediately delegates to the parent class constructor, passing the formatted string `"${count}"` so that the rendered placeholder reflects the positional number supplied [[target/app/db/queries/tables.py::Parameter::__init__]]. No additional fields are declared on the class itself, and no value is returned from construction nor are any exceptions raised [[target/app/db/queries/tables.py::Parameter::__init__]].

`TypedTable` is a subclass of pypika's `Table`, extending it with a class-level `__table__` attribute that defaults to an empty string [[target/app/db/queries/tables.py::TypedTable]]. It is not a Pydantic model [[target/app/db/queries/tables.py::TypedTable]]. Its purpose is to allow subclasses to declare their database table name declaratively via `__table__`, rather than relying solely on the class name [[target/app/db/queries/tables.py::TypedTable]]. When constructing an instance, if no explicit `name` argument is provided, the constructor resolves the table name by falling back first to the class-level `__table__` attribute and, if that is also absent, to the class's own `__name__` [[target/app/db/queries/tables.py::TypedTable::__init__]]. The resolved name, together with `schema`, `alias`, and `query_cls`, is forwarded to the parent `Table` implementation via `super().__init__` [[target/app/db/queries/tables.py::TypedTable::__init__]].

`ArticlesRepository` is the data-access class responsible for all database operations relating to articles, and it inherits from `BaseRepository` [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository]] [[target/app/db/repositories/base.py::BaseRepository]]. It is not a Pydantic model. The class carries a `# noqa: WPS214` suppression, indicating it deliberately contains a higher-than-usual number of methods [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository]].

On construction, it forwards the database connection to its parent class and then creates two collaborating repositories — a `ProfilesRepository` and a `TagsRepository` — both sharing the same connection, so that article-level operations can delegate profile and tag lookups without opening separate connections [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::__init__]].

The private `_get_article_from_db_record` helper assembles a fully populated `Article` domain object from a raw database row, reading scalar fields directly from the row while accepting `slug` and `author_username` as separate parameters [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::_get_article_from_db_record]]. It fetches the author profile (forwarding a `requested_user` so follow state is reflected), retrieves associated tags and favorites count, and resolves the `favorited` flag only when a `requested_user` is present, defaulting to `False` otherwise [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::_get_article_from_db_record]].

The private `_link_article_with_tags` helper associates a sequence of tag strings with an article identified by its slug, writing one `{slug, tag}` mapping per tag through `queries.add_tags_to_article` [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::_link_article_with_tags]].

`create_article` persists a new article and its tags atomically inside a transaction — inserting the article row, ensuring all tags exist, linking them, and then hydrating a full `Article` domain object outside the transaction boundary before returning it [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::create_article]]. `update_article` deep-copies the existing `Article`, overlays any supplied field replacements, executes `queries.update_article` within a transaction using the original slug and author as lookup keys, and returns the modified copy [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::update_article]]. `delete_article` removes an article row from the database within a transaction, keyed by slug and author username [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::delete_article]].

`get_article_by_slug` fetches a single article row by slug and hydrates it into a domain object, raising `EntityDoesNotExist` if no matching row is found [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::get_article_by_slug]]. `filter_articles` builds a dynamic pypika query against the articles table — optionally joining on tags, author, or favorites — and returns a paginated list of hydrated `Article` objects, personalised for the `requested_user` [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::filter_articles]]. `get_articles_for_user_feed` queries for articles written by authors the requesting user follows, hydrating each raw row into a full `Article` before returning the list [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::get_articles_for_user_feed]].

The remaining methods handle tag and favorites data. `get_tags_for_article_by_slug` retrieves all tags for an article by slug, returning them as a flat list of strings [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::get_tags_for_article_by_slug]]. `get_favorites_count_for_article_by_slug` returns the integer count of how many users have favorited a given article [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::get_favorites_count_for_article_by_slug]]. `is_article_favorited_by_user` delegates to the query layer and returns the boolean result of the `"favorited"` key directly [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::is_article_favorited_by_user]]. `add_article_into_favorites` persists a favorite relationship between a user and an article, returning nothing on success [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::add_article_into_favorites]], and `remove_article_from_favorites` deletes that relationship using the same connection, username, and slug parameters [[target/app/db/repositories/articles.py::ArticlesRepository::remove_article_from_favorites]].

`BaseRepository` is a plain Python class (not a Pydantic model) that serves as the foundation for all database repository classes in the project [[target/app/db/repositories/base.py::BaseRepository]]. It declares no base classes of its own [[target/app/db/repositories/base.py::BaseRepository]].

At construction time it accepts an asyncpg `Connection` instance and stores it in the private attribute `_conn`, making it available to any subclass that needs to execute queries [[target/app/db/repositories/base.py::BaseRepository::__init__]]. A `connection` property exposes `_conn` as read-only access to that underlying `Connection` object, so subclasses can retrieve the active connection without directly referencing the private attribute [[target/app/db/repositories/base.py::BaseRepository::connection]].

`CommentsRepository` is a database repository class responsible for all comment-related persistence operations, extending `BaseRepository` [[target/app/db/repositories/comments.py::CommentsRepository]] [[target/app/db/repositories/base.py::BaseRepository]].
